1.name: introduce serrano house
1.description: The scene establishes the Serrano house as an old, long-standing home in Spring Garden.
evidence: The Serrano house stood on a block in Spring Garden where the trees were old enough to have learned to grow around the streetlamps, and the bricks had been laid before anyone living had been born.

1.name: reveal estela's reading window
1.description: Asha observes the second-floor bay window associated with Estela Serrano's habit of reading there in life.
evidence: From the sidewalk Asha could see the bay window on the second floor where, according to the obituary, Estela Serrano had liked to read in the afternoons until the last winter of her life, when the stairs became a country she could no longer cross alone.

1.name: notice open shutters
1.description: Asha sees that the shutters on the upstairs window are still open, implying someone inside has not closed them.
evidence: The shutters on that window were still open.
Whoever was inside had not yet learned to close a dead woman's curtains.

1.name: arrive after funeral
1.description: The narration places the visit on Tuesday, one week after Estela's funeral.
evidence: It was Tuesday, the week after the funeral.
1.time_hint: Tuesday, the week after the funeral

1.name: bring case file
1.description: Asha arrives carrying a leather portfolio containing the file, signaling a formal meeting she expects to go badly.
evidence: Asha had brought the file in a leather portfolio she carried only when she expected a meeting to go badly.

1.name: invoke father's advice
1.description: The portfolio's origin and Asha's father's advice reveal her inherited professional habits and family background.
evidence: The portfolio had belonged to her father, who had also been an attorney, and who had told her once that the only thing worth inheriting was a habit of taking notes when other people were performing.

1.name: ring doorbell
1.description: Asha climbs the stoop and presses the doorbell to announce her arrival.
evidence: She climbed the stoop in her low heels and pressed the brass button beside the door.
Somewhere inside, a bell with a real clapper rang.

1.name: rosa answers door
1.description: Rosa opens the door instead of the people Asha expected to meet.
evidence: Rosa opened the door.

1.name: expect different greeters
1.description: Asha is surprised that the housekeeper answers, since she had expected Daniel or Lucia.
evidence: Asha had not expected the housekeeper.
She had expected Daniel, who had called twice that morning, or Lucia, who had not called at all but whose name appeared in the file as a current resident.

1.name: describe rosa's presence
1.description: Rosa is described as an older, long-serving housekeeper whose appearance suggests years of routine and discipline.
evidence: Instead there was a woman in her late sixties in a navy cardigan, hair pulled back in a way that suggested it had been pulled back in exactly that way every morning for forty years.

1.name: Rosa admits Asha into the house
1.description: Rosa opens the door for Asha and grants her entry with quiet authority.
evidence: "Ms. Patel," Rosa said. It was not a question. "Come in. They are in the dining room. I made coffee."
"Thank you." Asha stepped into the vestibule.
She held the door with the unhurried authority of someone who had decided, long before this morning, who was allowed past her.

1.name: Asha arrives early for the meeting
1.description: Rosa notes that Asha has arrived eight minutes early, establishing the tense timing of the visit.
evidence: "You are early," Rosa said.
"By eight minutes."

1.name: Rosa warns Asha about the man waiting inside
1.description: Rosa tells Asha that a man has been waiting since dawn and will accuse her of being late.
evidence: "He will say you are late." Rosa's mouth did not move toward a smile, but something in the corner of her eye did.
"He has been here since seven. Walking the rooms. Counting."

1.name: Asha questions what he is counting
1.description: Asha asks what the man is counting, prompting Rosa to imply he is tallying what he believes he deserves.
evidence: "Counting what?"
"Whatever he thinks he is owed."

1.name: Rosa leads Asha toward the dining room
1.description: Rosa walks down the hall and Asha follows her deeper into the house toward the waiting group.
evidence: Rosa turned and started down the hall, and Asha followed her past a staircase whose banister had been polished so many times the mahogany looked liquid.
"They are in the dining room."

1.name: Rosa reveals she witnessed the will signing
1.description: Before they sit down, Rosa tells Asha she witnessed the señora's will four years ago and another change eight months ago.
evidence: "I will tell you something now, before you sit down, because once you sit down they will not let me speak. I was a witness for the señora when she signed her will, four years ago. I was a witness again, eight months ago, when she signed something else. A change."
1.time_hint: four years ago; eight months ago

1.name: witness reveals prior signing
1.description: The woman explains that she witnessed the señora sign her will four years earlier and another document eight months ago.
evidence: I was a witness for the señora when she signed her will, four years ago. I was a witness again, eight months ago, when she signed something else.
1.time_hint: four years ago; eight months ago

1.name: witness describes altered document
1.description: She says the later document was changed, signed at the kitchen table with a lawyer on the phone, and witnessed by her and Mrs. Kim.
evidence: A change. She wrote it with the lawyer on the telephone and signed it at the kitchen table. I signed under her name. So did the woman from across the street, Mrs. Kim.

1.name: witness says paper is missing
1.description: She admits she has not seen the paper since and says it is not the same document Mr. Halloran has in his office.
evidence: I have not seen the paper since. It is not the same paper Mr. Halloran has in his office.

1.name: witness warns before son speaks
1.description: She tells Asha she wants her to know this before the son starts talking.
evidence: I want you to know this before the son starts talking.

1.name: woman admits Asha into dining room
1.description: After speaking, the woman opens the pocket doors to the dining room and steps aside to let Asha enter.
evidence: then she pushed open the pocket doors to the dining room and stepped aside.

1.name: Asha absorbs witness statement
1.description: Asha has no time to respond and mentally files away the implications of the witness's account.
evidence: Asha did not have time to answer. She had time only to register the shape of what she had been handed — a witness, a remembered signing, a missing document — and to file it behind her sternum the way she had been trained to file things until she could look at them properly.

1.name: Daniel greets Asha
1.description: Daniel stands at the head of the dining table and greets Asha with a relieved smile, asking her to sit and ordering coffee.
evidence: Daniel was standing at the head of the dining table.
"Ms. Patel. Thank God. Sit, please. Coffee? Rosa, coffee."

1.name: Asha declines coffee
1.description: Asha says she already has coffee, interrupting the offer as she takes in the room.
evidence: "I have coffee," Asha said.

1.name: Daniel greets Asha warmly
1.description: Daniel welcomes Asha into the house with a relieved smile and offers her coffee.
evidence: opened and produced a smile that was meant to look like relief.
"Ms. Patel. Thank God. Sit, please. Coffee? Rosa, coffee."

1.name: Asha notices coffee already prepared
1.description: Asha points out that coffee is already waiting on the sideboard, revealing Rosa prepared it before Daniel asked.
evidence: "I have coffee," Asha said.
There was already a tray on the sideboard, a silver pot, three cups, cream in a small pitcher, sugar in a bowl with a tiny spoon.
Rosa had made it before Asha arrived, before Daniel asked.

1.name: Daniel fails to notice Rosa's preparation
1.description: Daniel does not seem to register that coffee was already made, suggesting his inattentiveness or preoccupation.
evidence: Rosa had made it before Asha arrived, before Daniel asked. Daniel did not appear to notice.

1.name: Lucia sits withdrawn at the table
1.description: Lucia is introduced as visibly upset and recently crying, holding a mug apart from the prepared tray.
evidence: Lucia was sitting at the far end of the table with her hands wrapped around a mug that was not from the tray.
She was younger than her brother by perhaps six years, dark-haired, wearing a black sweater and jeans, no makeup, the skin under her eyes the color of a bruise that had begun to yellow.
She had been crying recently enough that her voice, when she said "Hi," came out at half its usual register.

1.name: Asha greets Lucia and sits between them
1.description: Asha returns Lucia's greeting and takes a seat positioned between Daniel and Lucia while opening her portfolio.
evidence: "Hi," Asha said back, and took a seat at the side of the table, equidistant from each of them.
She set the portfolio down and opened it without looking at the contents

1.name: Asha studies the room instead of the portfolio
1.description: Asha deliberately avoids looking at the portfolio contents because she already knows them and wants to observe the people in the room.
evidence: because she already knew what was in it and she wanted to watch the room instead.

1.name: Daniel explains the unusual house meeting
1.description: Daniel says he appreciates Asha coming to the house and frames the meeting as necessary for discussing matters in context.
evidence: "I appreciate you coming to the house. I know it isn't standard. But there are things here we need to discuss in context"

1.name: Daniel reveals Lucia has stayed home all week
1.description: Daniel begins to explain Lucia's situation, then revises his wording and says she has preferred to stay in the house this week.
evidence: "and frankly Lucia has been —"
He glanced at his sister and visibly chose another word.
"Lucia has preferred to stay in the house this week, and it seemed easier."

1.name: Asha agrees to the house visit
1.description: Asha reassures Daniel that the arrangement is fine and says she prefers to inspect the property in person.
evidence: "It's fine," Asha said. "I prefer to see the property in any case."

1.name: Asha agrees to inspect property
1.description: Asha says she prefers to see the property herself, accepting the visit despite Lucia staying home.
evidence: "Lucia has preferred to stay in the house this week, and it seemed easier."
"It's fine," Asha said. "I prefer to see the property in any case."

1.name: Daniel proposes accepting buyer offer
1.description: Daniel presents a buyer's increased offer and says he wants to accept it quickly.
evidence: "The buyer's agent has been in touch again. They're prepared to come up to seven-twenty. That's a strong number for this block in this condition. They want a thirty-day close. I'd like to accept."

1.name: Lucia objects to Daniel
1.description: Lucia interrupts Daniel when he says he wants to accept the offer.
evidence: "Daniel," Lucia said.

1.name: Daniel seeks probate guidance
1.description: Daniel repeats that he wants to accept the offer, framing it as contingent on Asha's probate advice and claiming the will is clear.
evidence: "I'd like to accept," he repeated, to Asha, as if his sister had not spoken, "subject obviously to your guidance on probate timing. Halloran told me the will is clean and that there's no reason we can't move."

1.name: Asha tests the will understanding
1.description: Asha pauses the conversation and asks Daniel and Lucia to confirm their understanding of the 2020 will and its terms.
evidence: "Mr. Serrano," she said. "Before we talk about offers, I'd like to confirm what's in front of us. The will I have is the one your mother executed in 2020. It leaves the house and contents jointly to the two of you, in equal shares, with you named as executor. Is that your understanding?"

1.name: Daniel confirms will terms
1.description: Daniel agrees that Asha's description of the will matches his understanding.
evidence: "Yes."

1.name: Lucia hesitates over will details
1.description: Lucia avoids directly answering Asha's question, first deferring to Halloran's copy of the will.
evidence: "Lucia. Is that your understanding?"
Lucia opened her mouth. Closed it. Looked down at her mug. "That's the will Mr. Halloran has, yes."

1.name: Asha presses Lucia for direct answer
1.description: Asha rejects Lucia's evasive reply and asks again for a direct confirmation.
evidence: "That isn't quite what I asked."

1.name: Lucia hardens emotionally
1.description: Lucia looks up with a changed expression, suggesting her grief has turned into something colder and harder.
evidence: Lucia looked up. Her eyes were not red anymore; they had passed through red into something flatter and harder

1.name: lucia confirms halloran has the will
1.description: Lucia states that the will in question is the one Mr. Halloran has.
evidence: "That's the will Mr. Halloran has, yes."
"It's the will Mr. Halloran has."

1.name: daniel challenges lucia's answer
1.description: Daniel presses Lucia for a clearer answer and accuses her of avoiding the question.
evidence: "That isn't quite what I asked."
"Lucia." Daniel's voice was the voice of a man who had been managing his sister since she was eight.
"Don't do this. Don't make it complicated.

1.name: daniel invokes mother's illness
1.description: Daniel argues that their mother was sick and medicated at the end, suggesting her wishes may not have been reliable.
evidence: "Mom was sick. She was on a lot of medication at the end."
"If you have feelings about what she might have wanted, we can talk about them, but feelings aren't documents."

1.name: lucia denies emotional argument
1.description: Lucia rejects Daniel's framing and insists she did not mention feelings.
evidence: "I didn't say anything about feelings."
"I didn't imply anything. I answered Ms. Patel's question."

1.name: asha interrupts the argument
1.description: Asha raises a finger to stop the siblings from talking over each other and regain control of the conversation.
evidence: "Asha lifted one finger half an inch off the table. Both of them stopped."
"It was a small trick and it worked on most families, at least the first time."

1.name: asha asks about modifying documents
1.description: Asha asks whether any formal or informal document, note, draft, or written conversation could alter the 2020 will.
evidence: "Let me ask it differently," she said.

"Is there any document, formal or informal, that either of you is aware of that might modify the terms of the 2020 will? A letter, a note, a draft, a conversation that was reduced to writing. Anything."

1.name: daniel denies any modifying document
1.description: Daniel immediately says he knows of no document that would change the will.
evidence: "No."

1.name: lucia hints at invalid statements
1.description: Lucia answers cautiously that she knows of nothing valid, implying she may have heard their mother say things that were not formalized.
evidence: "Not that I know is valid."
"I don't know what's valid. That's her job."
"I'm not going to sit here and pretend I never heard Mom say things."

1.name: daniel reacts sharply to lucia
1.description: Daniel turns on Lucia angrily after her qualified answer, signaling tension and suspicion between them.
evidence: "Daniel turned to look at his sister so sharply that the legal pad slid an inch."
"Lucia."

1.name: Lucia challenges validity of mother's statements
1.description: Lucia refuses to accept the attorney's framing and says she has heard their mother say things before.
evidence: "s valid. I don't know what's valid. That's her job." Lucia tilted her head at Asha without looking at her. "I'm not going to sit here and pretend I never heard Mom say things."

1.name: Lucia mentions mother's joke about silver
1.description: Lucia provokes the room by repeating that their mother once said she would leave the silver to the cat.
evidence: "Mom said a lot of things. Mom said she was going to leave the silver to the cat."

1.name: Asha shuts down Lucia's provocation
1.description: Asha repeatedly tells Lucia to stop, signaling rising tension in the room.
evidence: "Don't."
"Don't."

1.name: Rosa remains detached from the argument
1.description: An uneasy silence passes, and Rosa stays focused on work while the others tense up.
evidence:
"There was a pause in which something old and ugly moved through the room and lay down again under the table. Asha breathed out very slowly through her nose.

"Rosa," she said, without turning. "Would you sit, please."

"I am working," Rosa said.

1.name: Asha asks Rosa to sit
1.description: Asha directs Rosa to take a seat, shifting the focus of the conversation toward her.
evidence: "Rosa," she said, without turning. "Would you sit, please."
"I would like you to sit."

1.name: Rosa chooses a neutral seat
1.description: Rosa sits between the attorney and the siblings, positioning herself at an equal distance from everyone.
evidence: Rosa came around the table, considered the empty chair across from Asha, and instead pulled out the chair to Asha's left, which placed her between the attorney and neither sibling, equidistant from all of them. She sat with her hands folded in her lap and her back straight and waited.

1.name: Asha questions Rosa about witnessing documents
1.description: Asha begins formal questioning by asking how long Rosa worked for Mrs. Serrano and whether she witnessed documents for her.
evidence: "Rosa," Asha said. "How long did you work for Mrs. Serrano?"
"And in that time, did you witness any documents on her behalf?"

1.name: Rosa reveals she witnessed two documents
1.description: Rosa states that she worked for Mrs. Serrano for thirty-one years and witnessed her will and another paper.
evidence: "Thirty-one years in June."
"Twice. Her will, in 2020. And another paper, last October."

1.name: Daniel objects angrily to Rosa's testimony
1.description: Daniel explodes at the implication of Rosa's statement and starts to challenge her credibility.
evidence: "Oh, for fuck's —" Daniel pushed back from the table.
"Rosa, I don't know what you think you saw, but you are not a lawyer, and my mother was on three different medications by October, and —"

1.name: Asha orders Daniel to sit down
1.description: Asha cuts Daniel off and commands him to sit, asserting control over the exchange.
evidence: "Mr. Serrano," Asha said. "Sit down."

1.name: Daniel resists before yielding to Asha
1.description: Daniel remains standing in anger, then sits only because Asha uses a voice that compels him.
evidence: He did not sit down. He stood with his hands on the back of the chair and his knuckles white.
Daniel sat down. He sat down because Asha had used the voice she

1.name: Daniel challenges the legal claim
1.description: Daniel argues that the speaker misread the situation and is not a lawyer, while invoking his mother's medications to dispute the implication.
evidence: "think you saw, but you are not a lawyer, and my mother was on three different medications by October, and —"

1.name: Asha orders Daniel to sit
1.description: Asha uses an authoritative tone to cut off Daniel and make him sit down.
evidence: "Mr. Serrano. Sit down."
Daniel sat down.

1.name: Daniel suppresses his anger
1.description: Daniel obeys Asha's command but does so angrily, masking his fury with a hand over his face.
evidence: He sat down because Asha had used the voice she had been taught, in her first year of practice, by a judge who had told her that the only authority a young woman would ever have in a room of older men was the authority she took without asking.
He sat down, and he was furious about sitting down, and he covered the fury with a hand passed over his face.

1.name: Asha asks about the paper
1.description: Asha presses Rosa to explain what the document said.
evidence: "Rosa," Asha said. "What did the paper say."

1.name: Rosa describes the will change
1.description: Rosa says she did not read the paper carefully but was told it was a change to the señora's will concerning the house.
evidence: "I did not read it carefully. I am not the kind to read other people's papers. The señora told me it was a change to her will. She said the house was the question. She said she wanted to be sure."

1.name: Lawyer dictates and paper is signed
1.description: Rosa explains that another lawyer spoke by phone, the señora wrote and read the document aloud, and multiple people signed it.
evidence: "The lawyer, not Mr. Halloran but another man, was on the telephone. She wrote on a piece of paper. She read it aloud. She signed at the bottom. I signed. Mrs. Kim from across the street signed."

1.name: Document is stored in sewing room drawer
1.description: Rosa says the señora placed the signed paper in a folder and hid it in the bottom drawer of her desk in the sewing room.
evidence: "The señora put the paper in a folder and the folder in the bottom drawer of her desk in the sewing room."

1.name: Asha clarifies the sewing room
1.description: Asha identifies the sewing room as the small back room upstairs where the señora kept her machine and paid bills.
evidence: "The sewing room."
"The small room on the second floor at the back. Where she kept her machine. She did her bills there."
1.location_hint: small room on the second floor at the back

1.name: Asha asks whether the folder was searched
1.description: Asha asks Rosa if she has looked for the folder since the señora died.
evidence: "Have you looked for the folder since she died?"

1.name: Rosa refuses to search the house
1.description: Rosa says she has not looked for the folder because the house is not hers and she no longer works there.
evidence: "No."
"Because it is not my house," Rosa said, "and I am not employed here anymore."

1.name: Daniel ends Rosa's employment
1.description: Rosa reveals that Daniel told her last Friday her services would no longer be needed after the funeral.
evidence: "Mr. Serrano informed me last Friday that my services would not be required after the funeral."

1.name: Lucia summons Rosa to testify
1.description: Rosa says she came to the meeting because Miss Lucia asked her to come.
evidence: "I came today because Miss Lucia asked me to come."

1.name: speaker says employment has ended
1.description: The speaker explains that Mr. Serrano told her last Friday that her services would no longer be needed after the funeral.
evidence: Mr. Serrano informed me last Friday that my services would not be required after the funeral.

1.name: speaker explains why she came
1.description: The speaker says she came today because Miss Lucia asked her to come.
evidence: I came today because Miss Lucia asked me to come.

1.name: Asha closes her eyes briefly
1.description: Asha briefly closes her eyes, suggesting strain or resignation.
evidence: Asha allowed herself, briefly, to close her eyes.

1.name: Daniel shows visible distress
1.description: When Asha opens her eyes, Daniel appears visibly affected, with a small white patch at each temple.
evidence: When she opened them, Daniel had developed a small white patch at each temple

1.name: Lucia braces herself on the table
1.description: Lucia places both hands flat on the table as if steadying herself against an emotional shock.
evidence: Lucia had put both her hands flat on the table as if she were bracing for the house to tilt.
